name: Xiaomi Redmi Note 9 Pro / 9S
summary: ztOS on the Redmi Note 9 Pro (joyeuse) and Redmi Note 9S (curtana), Snapdragon 720G, without postmarketOS. Mainline Linux 6.14.7 from sm7125-mainline, with a fix for the speaker amplifier's volume and Landlock for pacman. Xiaomi's bootloader starts U-Boot from BOOT, then systemd-boot on CACHE, the kernel and ztOS's boot stage; the system lives in USERDATA. Display, touch, the Adreno GPU, Wi-Fi, the speaker and charging (at 1.4 A) work; the modem DSP runs, but calls, SMS, data and the sensors are not set up yet. Built on Linux in a user namespace, no root needed.
specs: 2× Kryo 465 Gold at 2.3 GHz, 6× Kryo 465 Silver at 1.8 GHz

install.markdown:
> **This erases the phone.** ztOS writes USERDATA, CACHE, DTBO and BOOT. It
> never touches the IMEI, the modem's partitions or persist.

For the Redmi Note 9 Pro (`joyeuse`) and 9S (`curtana`), not the 5G.

## What you need

- A Linux computer with 30 GB free
- A USB-C data cable, and the phone charged above 50%

## 1. Install the tools on your computer

```sh
sudo pacman -S --needed git python clang lld llvm bc ccache flex bison pahole \
  dtc dosfstools mtools cpio e2fsprogs libarchive android-tools qemu-user-static qemu-user-static-binfmt
```

## 2. Get ztOS

```sh
git clone https://github.com/cyber-dream/ztOS-miatoll.git
cd ztOS-miatoll
installer/ztos doctor
```

## 3. Unlock the bootloader

1. In MIUI: Developer options > **Mi Unlock status**, bind your Mi account.
2. In fastboot (Volume Down + Power), unlock with Xiaomi's **Mi Unlock** tool. It may ask you to wait some days.

## 4. Install ztOS

```sh
mkdir -p build && echo joyeuse-huaxing > build/miatoll-variant   # or curtana-, -tianma
devices/xiaomi-miatoll/kernel/build-kernel.sh
installer/ztos build --target miatoll --user YOURNAME --password YOURPASSWORD
devices/xiaomi-miatoll/scripts/flash.sh    # phone in fastboot
```

The build takes about 1–1½ hours the first time.

## 5. Start ztOS

The first start takes about a minute. Then log in with your user name and
password. Over USB: `ssh YOURNAME@172.16.42.1`.

Save the phone's own partitions once with
`devices/xiaomi-miatoll/scripts/backup.sh YOURNAME@172.16.42.1`.

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What to do |
|---|---|
| A black screen, but `ssh` works | Your phone has the other panel: write `joyeuse-tianma` to `build/miatoll-variant`, run `devices/xiaomi-miatoll/boot/build-boot.sh` and `flash.sh --boot-only` |
| `the battery is too low for the bootloader` | Charge it switched off for half an hour |
| `pacman` times out | Put `Server = http://de.mirror.archlinuxarm.org/$arch/$repo` first in `/etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist` |
| Back to Android | Flash Xiaomi's fastboot ROM with its `flash_all.sh` |

notes.title: Charging is slow, and only up to 1.4 A.
notes.text: Linux has no driver for the PM6150's charger yet; the PMIC charges on its own at the input limit the bootloader sets. A long charge takes a few hours; a 9 V fast charger charges at 5 V.

notes.title: Settings shows the Galaxy S9's processor and graphics.
notes.text: Its processor, graphics and About pages are written for the S9 (Exynos 9810, Mali-G72). The phone's own facts are in its ztOSIAL manifest, for when Settings reads them.

notes.title: The clock is wrong after a restart without internet.
notes.text: The PMIC's clock is not kept; it starts at the build's date until NTP sets it.

notes.title: No sound, while the volume panel says Headphones.
notes.text: The volume panel's output switch also offers the headphones when none are plugged in, and the choice is kept per app. Switch back to Speaker there.

notes.title: A wrong battery level for a minute after a restart.
notes.text: The fuel gauge needs a minute to settle; it corrects itself.
